2-7-p026-07|BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Spe.annotation: Each alternative has its own Lean constructor with a byte-sequence payload. In particular a numeral stores its digits, and a string stores its content. Their interpretation as terms is supplied by the relevant theory (see Remark 1 on special constants).

2-7-p027-03|BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Ind.annotation: Both alternatives satisfy `Index.Valid` in version 2.7. The version check is relevant to symbolic indices, which this implementation admits from 2.5 onward. The characters of a numeral or symbol are handled by the lexicon (see Section 3.1 for the spelling rules).

2-7-p028-03|BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Sor.annotation: For each sort node, `Valid` checks the identifier's indices and recursively checks the argument subtrees. The predicate has no signature parameter for checking declared arities (see Definition 1, Sorts).

2-7-p030-01|BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Ter.annotation: In the application case, `Valid` requires at least one argument and checks the qualified identifier and each argument for grammatical validity. The predicate has no binder environment or function signature, so variables and function ranks are resolved outside this check (see Section 3.6.3 on well-sortedness).

2-7-p030-06|BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Pat.annotation: The `.single` branch contains a symbol or wildcard. The `.constructor` branch stores a constructor name and a list of symbol-or-wildcard arguments (see Remark 5 on nested patterns), with the requirement of at least one argument imposed by `Pattern.Valid`.

2-7-p031-02|BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Ter.annotation: For a binder such as `let`, `Valid` checks the grammar of the bindings and the body. Free and bound occurrences are described separately in Section 3.6.2 of the standard, and no assignment from names to their binders appears in this predicate.

The token function preserves the written positions of binders, names and bodies. For example it emits a `let` binding list before the body. The standard (Section 3.6.2) gives separate scope rules for identifying the occurrences that refer to each binding.

2-7-p031-03|BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Ter.annotation: A lambda node with two variables becomes a single `lambda` followed by a list with two entries and then the body. These are the tokens of the abbreviated form in Equation (3.1) before the expansion written in Equation (3.2).

2-7-p031-07|BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Ter.annotation: Both quantifiers use the same check for a nonempty list of sorted variables and a grammatically valid body. The standard's expansion into nested quantifiers (Equation (3.4) for `forall`) belongs to the interpretation of the resulting expression.

2-7-p031-07|BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Sor.annotation: Each quantified variable contributes a group such as `(x Int)`. The quantified-term branch collects the groups into one variable list before the body, as in the single `forall` of Equation (3.3).

2-7-p032-10|BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Ter.annotation: The `match` branch writes the term to be matched first, then a parenthesized list of cases in order. The function emits this syntax for a given tree. Selecting a case is part of evaluation (see the `match` expansion at Equation (3.7)).

2-7-p033-01|BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Ter.annotation: The helper checks each pair's pattern and result term separately. There is no datatype or expected result sort among its inputs, so coverage of the datatype and agreement of result sorts lie outside the check (see the two `match` rules in Figure 5.3).

2-7-p033-05|BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Pat.annotation: After the constructor name, `Pattern.tokens` maps a one-token function over the arguments. There is no recursive call for an argument, reflecting the flat constructor patterns described in Remark 5.

2-7-p036-07|BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Qua.annotation: In the `.as` case, `Valid` asks whether $f$ is a grammatically valid identifier and $\tau$ a grammatically valid sort expression. The requirement in Remark 8 that $\tau$ match a declared result sort needs the function's rank as well.

The function can write a supplied identifier and sort in the `as` form without looking up the identifier. It accounts for the spelling in Remark 8, where the required agreement with the declared return sort is a semantic condition.

2-7-p051-04|BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Dat.annotation: The nonempty constructor condition supplies the plus shared by both alternatives. The same predicate checks the grammar of every constructor. Sort parameters and constructor arities are checked against the surrounding declarations when interpreting the datatype (see `declare-datatypes` in Section 4.2.3).

2-7-p105-10|BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.keyword|.annotation: The appendix refers to the entire simple-symbol rule after the colon. Lean instead calls for a nonempty letter, digit or punctuation sequence. It therefore admits `:56` (printed under Keywords in Section 3.1) and `:let`, following the older rule documented beside `keyword`.
